operations.summary: Search the product-research catalog by filter.
operations.notes:
Read-only POST. Searches the product-research catalog and returns `{results: [...], region, currency}`. Winning products and deleted products are excluded automatically.

The body is a filter object. `order_by` ({name, direction}) and `filters` are both REQUIRED. `filters` is a list of {name, value, value_type, op}, all combined with AND; an unfiltered listing is `filters: []` — a body with no `filters` key at all is refused before the call is made, because the upstream answers that shape with an error rather than a listing. The whole filter vocabulary, with the `value_type` and `op` each field takes, is documented on the `filters[].name` parameter; the three most useful: free text is `{name: "search_query", value_type: "string", op: "search"}`, the AutoDS Marketplace is `{name: "site_name", value: "private_suppliers", value_type: "list", op: "in"}`, and a category is `{name: "categories.autods_category_id.$id", value_type: "objectId", op: "="}` with an id from `get_categories` (a parent id matches every product in its whole subtree). `region` is resolved from the user's settings server-side and is ignored if sent.

Three things about the response a caller gets wrong otherwise:

- **Results are card-shaped, not full products.** Each result carries 12 fields — the ids, `title`, `images`, `categories`, `site_name`, `supplier_name`, `private_supplier`, `product_details` and the winning-product flags. Fields you can *filter* on are not all fields you *get back*: `rating`, `description`, `brand`, `url` and the per-variation details are absent here. Call `get_product_by_id` with a result's `_id` for the full document.
- **No total count is returned.** Page with `offset`/`limit` (default limit 10) and stop on an empty page — but read the next bullet before treating a short page as the end.
- **Paging ends at 10,000 results, and the final page comes back short rather than empty.** An `offset` beyond that window is refused as `invalid_arguments` (it is capped at 9999 in this schema), but a page that merely runs past the ceiling from inside the window is silently truncated instead — `offset: 9999, limit: 2` returns one result. So a short page near the ceiling is not proof the catalog is exhausted; narrow the filters instead of paging on.

body_schema.description: Product-research search filter. `order_by` and `filters` are both required; `filters: []` is the unfiltered listing.

offset.description: Pagination offset, capped at 9999 — the last item of the 10,000-result window. A larger `offset` is refused here as `invalid_arguments` rather than reaching the upstream. A page that runs past the window from inside it is not refused: it comes back short (`offset: 9999, limit: 2` returns one result), so the ceiling shows up as a short page and never as an error.

limit.description: Page size (default 10, max 50). A result is roughly 2KB, so a large page can exhaust the client's context in a single call.

name.description: Field to sort by. Sortable: created_at, product_details.min_price, product_details.min_shipping_time, spv_param (relevance), view_count. A text field is not sortable — `title` is refused as an `upstream_client_error`.

filters.description: Filter conditions, every one of them combined with AND. Required, and an empty list is how an unfiltered listing is requested: send `filters: []`, never a body without the key.

name.description:
Field to filter on. Each entry below names the `value_type` and `op` it takes.
- `search_query` (string, `search`) — free text, matched against title, description and supplier name. This is also how to reach a supplier whose exact name you do not have.
- `site_name` (list, `in`; or string with `=` for a single channel, `ne` to exclude one) — the sales channel a product was sourced from. `private_suppliers` is the AutoDS Marketplace / private-supplier channel, and is NOT the same as `shopify`, which is independently scraped Shopify storefronts.
- `supplier_name` (string, `=`) — exact, case-sensitive, full-string match. There is no partial match and nothing lists the suppliers, so the name has to come from an earlier result; for anything less than exact use `search_query`.
- `private_supplier.product_condition` (string, `=`) — `new` or `used`.
- `private_supplier.is_logo_invoice_allowed` (bool, `=`) — `true`/`false`; white-label invoicing.
- `private_supplier.store_type` (string, `=`) — `shopify`.
- `private_supplier.map_percent` (integer, `=`/`<`/`>`) — minimum-advertised-price percentage.
  Every `private_supplier.*` filter implicitly restricts the search to Marketplace products, whether or not `site_name` is also filtered.
- `variations.variation_details.price` (float, `between`/`<`/`>`) — item price.
- `variations.variation_details.min_shipping_time` (integer, `<`) — shipping time in days.
- `variations.variation_details.warehouse` (list, `in`) — ships-from: the country the item ships out of, not the destination. Values: ALL, US, CN, AU, CA, DE, ES, FR, IT, UK, PL, RU, BE, NL, CZ, TH, BR.
- `categories.autods_category_id.$id` (objectId, `=`) — a category id from `get_categories`. A parent id matches every product anywhere in its subtree, so filter by the broadest category that fits the intent instead of collecting leaf ids.
- `_id` (objectId, `=`) — one product by id.
- `rating` (float, `>`) and `rating_count` (integer, `>`) — set only on products sourced outside the Marketplace, so combining either with `site_name` = `private_suppliers` matches nothing at all rather than filtering.

value.description: Operand, always sent as a string and cast per `value_type`. `between` takes exactly two comma-separated bounds (`"20,25"`) — the `min-max` dash form documented on `get_winning_products` is not accepted here. `in` takes a comma-separated list (`"US,CN"`). The values a particular field accepts are listed with that field under `name`.

value_type.description: How to read `value`: use the type of the field being filtered — `float` for prices, `integer` for counts and day windows, `objectId` for a 24-character hex id, `list` for a comma-separated `in` operand, `bool` for `true`/`false`, `string` otherwise.

op.description: Comparison. `search` is only for `search_query`; `between` needs two comma-separated bounds; `in` takes a comma-separated list.

operations.summary: List winning products with optional discovery filters.
operations.notes: Read-only. Returns {results: [...]} of winning products. `offset`, `limit` (1-100) and `sort` are required. `sort` is a field name; prefix with `-` for descending (e.g. -created_at, -orders_count). Optional filters: category (24-character hex id), ads (advertising platform name, e.g. Facebook/TikTok), orders (min order count), profit / item_cost (range buckets like 10-20 or 100-), created_date (day window: 0=today,1,7,14,30), search (free text). Without the Product Finding Hub subscription the service returns a limited free set.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field; prefix with '-' for descending, e.g. -created_at.

parameters.name: ads
parameters.description: Advertising platform name(s), comma-separated, e.g. Facebook,TikTok.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search across title, description, or supplier.

operations.summary: Get a single product by its id.
operations.notes: Read-only. Returns the full product document for the given product id (24-character hex string), with prices/region normalised to the user's settings. A winning product the caller is not entitled to see (no Product Finding Hub add-on) is refused upstream with a redirect, which this tool reports as an `upstream_error` about an "unexpected redirect" — that error means the entitlement is missing, not that the id is wrong or the service is down, so do not retry it and do not report a fault: say the product needs the Product Finding Hub add-on. `get_winning_products` still returns the limited free set without it.

operations.summary: Get products similar to the given product.
operations.notes: Read-only. Returns {results: [...]} of products similar to the given product id (same region/categories, excluding winning and deleted products), preferring the same private supplier. Up to ~20 results.

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: Product id (24-character hex string) to find similar products for.

operations.summary: Get products recommended for the given product.
operations.notes: Read-only. Returns {results: [...], total_results} of products recommended for the given product id, with prices normalised to the user's currency/region. Use `offset`/`limit` for pagination (default limit 10).

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: Product id (24-character hex string) to base recommendations on.

operations.description: Return the whole AutoDS product category tree in one call. Read-only, takes no parameters. This is how a category the user named becomes an id the `search_products` category filter can take.
operations.notes:
Returns `{results: [...]}`: a tree of `{value, label, children}` nodes, top-level categories first, each leaf carrying an empty `children` list. The whole tree arrives in one response — there is no paging, and no way to request a single branch.

`value` is a 24-character hex id and is the only unique key in the tree. It is exactly what the `search_products` category filter takes: `{name: "categories.autods_category_id.$id", value: "<value>", value_type: "objectId", op: "="}`.

`label` is NOT unique, and treating it as unique is the mistake this tool invites. A label is unique only among its immediate siblings: `Clothing`, `Pants`, `Shorts`, `Shoes` and `Accessories` each exist separately under `Women`, `Men`, `Girls` and `Boys`, and `Mirrors` exists under two unrelated parents. What identifies a category is its position in the tree, so resolve one by walking down from the top-level category that matches the intent — never by matching a label anywhere in the tree, which silently picks one of several unrelated categories and returns a confident wrong answer with no error.

Filtering by a parent id matches every product anywhere in that parent's subtree, not only products filed directly under it. So filter by the broadest category that fits the intent: one id near the top of the tree covers everything below it, and there is no need to collect the ids of its descendants.

`Other Category` is the catch-all and is always the last top-level entry; it has no children.

The tree changes a few times a year, so call this once per task and reuse the answer.
